newsitem.title: LATVIA: Transport Fleet sinks in slow Latvia share trade.
newsitem.headline: Transport Fleet sinks in slow Latvia share trade.

text.p: Latvian stocks showed more signs of stagnation on Thursday as volume remained stable and no immediate growth was expected, dealers said.
Total volume came to 167,000 lats against 161,000 lats and Rietmu Bank's bourse index fell 2.45 percent to 196.17.
"Stocks are little by little starting to stagnate and there are no expectations of growth in sight," Leonid Ruderman of Parex Bank said. "Prices are stable to lower."
Riga Transport Fleet, an official list stock, sank some 15 percent to 1.42 lats on 7,800 lats of volume.
"It seems that one buyer of Fleet's shares, which supported its price throughout April, has now turned into a seller," Ruderman said.
Unibanka regained some ground after its dividend payments, advancing to 3.80 lats from 3.78 lats as it registered the bourse's largest trade of 48,300 lats.

Daugavpils Chain on the secondary list remained stable at 2.79 and had volume of 39,400 lats as the market now awaits the shareholders decision on bonus shares. The company has proposed a bonus issue of 84 shares for every 100 held.
Kaija fish cannery registered a small but a steady gain for the third consecutive day as it was lifted news it would be joining the official list soon.
The cannery added another three santimes to 2.50 lats as shares worth 21,000 lats changed hands.
Brasa furniture factory was also in demand on volume of 15,700 lats. It closed three santimes up at 0.29 santimes.
Elsewhere on the secondary list, Lode Brick, Valmiera Glassfibre and Liepaja fish cannery were actively traded.
Lode Brick traded 6,400 lats of shares and nudged down one santime to 2.60 lats while Valmiera had volume of 6,100 lats as it slipped three santimes to 1.82 lats.
Liepaja remained stable at 1.50 lats on trade of 5,200 lats.
